prime.problem: Standard attention writes the N×N scores S and probabilities P to HBM and reads them back. At 8k tokens that is 8.59 GB per Llama layer for S + P alone, all of it memory-bound traffic, and at 128k it is 27× the whole GPU.
prime.fits: Card 1 of 3 on FlashAttention. It applies the previous card's (m, ℓ) merge to whole tiles of the score matrix, so the N×N matrices live only in SRAM, one tile at a time.
expect: SRAM vs HBM (19 vs 1.5 TB/s on A100)
Algorithm 0: S and P written to HBM
tiling with running (m, ℓ) and a rescaled O
kernel fusion: one kernel, only O written
prime.goal: Walk through Algorithm 1's inner step, say what is stored in HBM and what never leaves SRAM, and explain why doing more FLOPs still makes it faster.

attend: Softmax couples every column of a row. What two numbers per row let FlashAttention finish a row it only ever sees one block at a time?
At each (i, j) step, which three things are read from HBM and written back, and which Br × Bc matrix never leaves SRAM?
When a new K block raises a row's max, why must O_i be rescaled by the same factor as ℓ_i?
How does the block-size rule B_c = ⌈M/4d⌉ follow from what has to fit in SRAM, and why is it a proof device rather than a tuning recipe?
Why is "recompute S and P in the backward pass" faster here, when ordinary checkpointing trades speed for memory?

must: S and P are N×N → writing and re-reading them makes attention memory-bound → split Q, K, V into SRAM-sized blocks and compute each S_ij on chip → fold it into O with running (m, ℓ) → S and P never reach HBM → O(N) extra memory instead of O(N²)

A new block may raise a row's max → the old ℓ_i and O_i were built on the old max → scale both by e^(m_old − m_new), add the block's e^(S−m)·V → after every step O_i is exact for the columns seen so far (Theorem 1, induction over j)

Keep only O and (m, ℓ) from the forward pass → rebuild S and P tile by tile in backward → +13% FLOPs but 9.2× less HBM traffic (GPT-2 medium: 40.3 → 4.4 GB) → 5.7× faster, because the bound was bytes, not FLOPs
elevated: FA1's loop order puts K, V outside and Q inside → O_i, ℓ_i, m_i round-trip to HBM on every (i, j) step → the waste FlashAttention-2 removes by swapping the loops
reference: Fig 1's exact bandwidths (19 TB/s estimated SRAM, 12.8 GB/s CPU DRAM)
the A100/H100 SRAM sizes (192 KB, 228 KB per SM)
the lab's trace values and error magnitudes

compress.prompt: Draw one tile step of Algorithm 1 from memory: which blocks come from HBM, what is computed in SRAM, which two statistics update, what gets rescaled, and what goes back to HBM. Then one line on why it's exact.
checklist: load K_j, V_j (outer) and Q_i, O_i, ℓ_i, m_i (inner)
S_ij = Q_i K_jᵀ on chip; block max, exp, block sum
new max and new ℓ; old ℓ and old O_i rescaled by e^(m_old − m_new)
write back O_i, ℓ_i, m_i only; S_ij and P̃_ij never
exact because the rescale only moves terms to a common reference point

retrieve.q: Explain what makes attention memory-bound in Algorithm 0 even though its matmuls are compute-heavy.
answer: S and P are N×N and each makes a round trip through HBM
softmax, masking and dropout are elementwise passes over N², with almost no FLOPs per byte
so HBM traffic, not the matmuls, sets the time once N ≫ d

retrieve.q: Trace row 0 of the lab's N = 512 run at block 2: the old max was 1.6232 and ℓ = 27.3275; the block's max is 2.7522 and its sum 13.5671. What is the new ℓ, and what happens to O_0?
answer: new max 2.7522; old terms scale by e^(1.6232 − 2.7522) = 0.3233
O_0 is scaled by the same 0.3233 before the block's P̃V is added, then divided by the new ℓ

retrieve.q: FlashAttention does 13% more FLOPs than standard attention. When would that extra arithmetic actually cost you time, and when is FlashAttention not the right tool at all?
answer: when the kernel is compute-bound (large blocks, long sequences), extra FLOPs do cost; the exp work bites again in FA3/FA4
in decode there is one query row and no N×N matrix to avoid
on small-SRAM GPUs (T4) the speedup shrinks
new attention variants need a new hand-written kernel

compare.q: Online softmax streams one vector; FlashAttention streams a whole attention row block by block. What does FlashAttention have to carry along that the vector version doesn't, and why does that make kernel fusion the real win?
answer: it must also rescale the running output O_i, a d-dimensional vector per row
with (m, ℓ, O) carried in SRAM, the matmul, softmax and second matmul can live in one kernel
fusion is what stops S and P from ever being written: the saving is IO, the trick is online softmax

compare.q: perf-3 tiled a transpose through shared memory to fix access patterns. What is the same about FlashAttention's tiling, and what is fundamentally different about why it needs tiles?
answer: same: stage blocks in on-chip SRAM so HBM is touched once per block
different: attention tiles exist to avoid materialising an intermediate (S, P) at all, not just to coalesce reads
that only works because softmax can be decomposed with (m, ℓ)

predict.q: Run Algorithm 1 exactly but delete the rescale factor e^(m_old − m_new) from both the ℓ and O updates. Is the error small (rounding) or large, and does it depend on the block size? Commit before revealing.
predict.answer: Large: the lab's try-this shows errors of about 0.1–0.5, not 10⁻⁷. Every time a later block raises a row's max, the old contributions stay measured against a smaller max, so they are overweighted by e^(m_new − m_old). It barely depends on block size as long as there are several blocks (our numpy check at N = 512, d = 128: max error 0.30, 0.32, 0.29, 0.31 for B_c = 16, 64, 114, 256), because the damage comes from the max rising at all. With one block covering the whole row (B_c = 512) the max never moves and the error falls to 9e-16.

apply.task: Size the tiles for an A100 (192 KB SRAM per SM, counted in 4-byte floats as the card does) and one Llama head (d = 128, N = 8,192): compute M, B_c, B_r, T_r × T_c and the number of inner-loop steps. Then compute, for 32 heads at N = 32,768 in BF16, what S + P would take per layer and what m + ℓ in FP32 take instead, and the ratio.
apply.done: You have M, the block sizes, the tile count, both memory figures and the ratio, each with one line of arithmetic, before opening the hint.
